problem:
The vectors ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$, and $b$ are given below. Determine if $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$ from the decomposition $b={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 7\end{aligned}]
$$

feedback.problem:
The vectors ${a}_{1}$, ${a}_{2}$, and $b$ are given below. Determine if $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$ from the decomposition $b={x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}.$

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ -7\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -6 \\ -11\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ -7\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -5\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -6 \\ -11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-1 \\ -4{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=-6 \\ -7{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=-11\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & -3 & -6 \\ -7 & -5 & -11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & -10 \\ -7 & -5 & -11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & -10 \\ 0 & 9 & -18\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 9 & -18\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-9{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-1 \\ {x}_{2}=-2 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-2.$ Substituting into the first equation gives 

$$
{x}_{1}+2(-2)=-1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=3.
$$

Since the system has a solution, we can conclude that $b\in \text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}.$

Moreover, there is exactly one solution, so we have exactly one way to write $b$ as a linear combination of ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3{a}_{1}+(-2){a}_{2} & =b \\ 3\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ -7\end{aligned}]+(-2)\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -5\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -6 \\ -11\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=3\cdot (-2)=-6.$
